segments.text: Excuse me, um, doctor, should I sit here?
Of course, put it down anywhere. So, how can I help?
Um, it's loose motions, mostly. My family kept telling me to get it checked.
Okay, and when did that start?
Since last night, that's when it began. I kept putting it off, which I know isn't sensible.
Alright, tell me a bit more about it: how bad it gets, how often, and whether anything makes it better or worse. It helps to be thorough at this stage.

It's, It's on and off. It's moderate, honestly. I just want to get back to normal, really. Oh, uh, and stomach cramps. Had that since this morning. About stomach cramps, a seven out of ten, I suppose. Right, I've been feeling weak too, for two days.
Let me check a few things. Any black stools, rash or blood in the stool?
Yeah, uh, no. None of those, no.
Okay, anyone in the family with similar problems or other conditions?
My grandmother had breast cancer.
What about operations, anything like that?
Yes, I had a stent put in my heart, two years ago. I've never really been one for hospitals.
Do you have any known allergies at all? Bear with me, I'm just building up the picture.
No, you know, nothing I'm aware of.
What medicines do you take regularly?
Glycomet, 500 milligrams, maybe, twice a day for my sugar.
Do you have the packet or the prescription with you?
Right, not with me. I'll bring it next time. Clopidogrel. I take it 75 milligrams, once a day for the stent. ORS, a few times a day.
Moving on to your background, any past medical history? Just so I get the full picture.
I've had diabetes, yes. Um, I have heart disease. I wasn't sure whether to come in at all, to be honest. I'm not great at remembering details, so bear with me.
Right, so that's your known diabetes. We'll keep that in mind today. I'll take a few measurements first.
Just relax your arm...
Okay: BMI works out to 20.3, height 172 centimetres, pulse 105. And weight 60 kilos, pressure 113 over 71, temperature 39.2.
Is that alright, doctor?
We'll put it in context in a moment.
Alright, I'd like to examine you now. Please come over here.
Hold your arm out like this.
You're mildly dehydrated.

All done, thank you, please sit down. Thank you for that. I'll write up what I found in a moment, and then I'll tell you what I think is going on. So, based on the history and the examination, I think we're dealing with acute gastroenteritis at this stage. It could also be food poisoning, so we'll keep that open.

We should do blood salts for dehydration. I'd rather check than guess, and this is the quickest way to know more. I'll start you on zinc, 20 milligrams, once a day, for ten days. It's for diarrhoea. Stick to bananas, rice, toast, curd, and avoid milk and oily food till it settles. Cut down on salt and fried food for now, it really does make a difference.
Cut back on tea, coffee and fizzy drinks for a couple of weeks and see how things settle. And please bring the latest prescription or the medicine boxes to the next visit, so we can settle the dose.
Okay, I will.
Keep an eye out, and if you pass blood or can't keep anything down, call us the same day or go to emergency. I'd like to see you again if it's not better in three days.
Okay, uh, I'll book that.
Right, we're all set. Don't leave without asking if something's unclear.
That's everything I wanted to ask. Thank you.
